profile.name: Ethan Prescott
profile.intro: I’m a mechanical engineering student at Villanova University and co-president of Villanova Club Robotics. I enjoy taking a project from a CAD model to a working build, solving the problems along the way, and working with a team to make it happen.
profile.interests: I’m interested in internship opportunities in robotics, mechanical design, and automation.

experience.title: Co-President

projects.title: FREEDOM
projects.subtitle: 3 lb NHRL combat robot
projects.summary: Led a nine-member team building one of Villanova’s first 3 lb combat robots to compete at NHRL.
projects.overview: FREEDOM is a 3 lb vertical-spinner combat robot built by Villanova Combat Robotics for competition at the National Havoc Robot League (NHRL). The project brought together mechanical design, component research, fabrication, electrical integration, and competition preparation.
projects.contribution: As team lead and driver, I coordinated mechanical and electrical subsystem development, delegated responsibilities, and managed project deadlines. My work included SolidWorks design iterations, component selection, weight-budget management, fabrication, and system integration.
projects.design: Collaborated across drivetrain, chassis, electronics, and rotating-system teams to resolve tradeoffs involving weight, packaging, reliability, and manufacturability within the 3 lb competition constraint.
projects.results: FREEDOM became one of Villanova’s first 3 lb combat robots to compete at NHRL. I served as its team lead and driver. More detailed competition notes and design iterations will be added here.

projects.title: Class Beetlebot
projects.subtitle: Beater-bar robot · Class weapons division
projects.summary: Designed and wired the control system for a beater-bar combat robot in the class weapons division, then drove it in competition with a three-person team.
projects.overview: A semester-long combat robot project for Mechanical Engineering Analysis and Design. Our three-person team built a robot for the weapons division, using a beater-bar weapon, and competed against other class teams.
projects.contribution: I served as lead project designer and driver, designed and wired the control system, and operated the robot during competition.
projects.design: The team’s robot used a beater-bar weapon for the class weapons division. My work focused on control-system design, wiring, and integration. Drawings and build photos will be added here.
projects.results: Drove the robot in the class weapons division, where our team defeated two competing robots.

projects.title: CTI Roller
projects.subtitle: Engineering internship project
projects.summary: Designed and fabricated a custom roller that doubled fiberglass-cutting efficiency during my engineering internship at CTI.
projects.overview: A custom roller built to improve the fiberglass-cutting workflow at Composite Technology and Infrastructure in Coeymans, New York.

projects.title: LimbLet
projects.subtitle: Wearable sensor venture concept
projects.summary: Developed a wearable sensor concept supporting preventive care for aging populations, from initial ideation to a venture pitch.
projects.overview: LimbLet is a wearable sensor concept developed through Villanova’s Engineering Entrepreneurship Summer Institute (E2SI) in Ireland. The concept aimed to support preventive care for aging populations.
projects.contribution: Collaborated with an interdisciplinary team of three to develop the concept and progress it from initial ideation to a venture pitch.
projects.design: Evaluated global innovation and sustainable business practices while in Ireland, incorporating recyclable materials and circular-economy principles into the product concept.
projects.results: Progressed the product concept into a venture pitch. This was a concept-stage project; a validated device or clinical result is not documented here.

projects.title: Iris+ Drone
projects.subtitle: Pixhawk setup & troubleshooting
projects.summary: Working on a 3DR Iris+ quadcopter: connecting the radio and flight controller, configuring telemetry, and troubleshooting motor and calibration issues.
projects.overview: An ongoing hands-on project working through the systems on a 3DR Iris+ quadcopter with a Pixhawk flight controller. The work covers the transmitter, receiver, telemetry radios, flight controller, and motors.
projects.contribution: Worked on receiver binding, radio calibration, neutral channel values, direct USB connection to Pixhawk, SiK telemetry setup, battery settings, and motor testing in Mission Planner.
projects.design: Investigated compass and pre-arm errors, radio connection issues, and differences in motor startup behavior. Used Mission Planner to inspect RC channel responses and test the system.
projects.results: RC input responses have been observed in Mission Planner. Motor startup and telemetry troubleshooting are ongoing; a successful flight has not yet been documented here.

projects.title: Eagle Scout Project
projects.subtitle: BioReserve conservation signs
projects.summary: Led the planning, fabrication, and installation of signs at the BioReserve, using protected wooden panels and welded metal joints to support conservation education.
projects.overview: For my Eagle Scout project, I worked with The Bioreserve, a nonprofit biological field reserve in Glenmont, New York, on signs about its historic or endangered plant life. Its leader previously relied on verbal guided tours to share information with visitors. The project added signs that could communicate that information on site, supporting tours and helping visitors learn from the signs themselves.
projects.contribution: Led project planning and communication, obtained approval from the Boy Scouts organization, and coordinated with the BioReserve to schedule installation. Worked alongside my dad and five friends and fellow Scouts. My dad helped source materials and arranged welding instruction from a friend; the team helped dig holes and install the signs.
projects.design: Selected affordable materials with long-term use at the preserve in mind. The signs used wooden panels with a protective coating, plus welded metal joints that positioned the panels at a comfortable reading angle. The project combined material sourcing, fabrication, welding instruction, and site installation.
projects.results: Installed signs that gave the BioReserve a lasting way to share information about its plant life without relying solely on verbal guided tours. Completing the project required balancing cost and durability, securing organizational approval, and coordinating volunteers and the preserve’s availability. The project formed part of earning my Eagle Scout rank.

projects.title: App made with AI
projects.subtitle: Quest · A private birthday game
projects.summary: Created Quest, a private birthday game with about a month of daily minigames, new games introduced over time, and personalized messages and rewards.
projects.overview: Quest is a private app I made for my girlfriend’s birthday. The experience spanned about a month, with minigames to play each day and additional minigames introduced as the days progressed. It included music, personal messages, rewards, Easter eggs, and difficulty features.
projects.contribution: I created the app myself using Base44’s AI development tools and independently playtested it. My work covered the game concept, daily experience, minigames, and personalized features.
projects.design: Built the experience through Base44, using its AI development tools to develop the minigames and supporting features. I organized the game around daily play, introduced new minigames over time, and playtested the app myself.
projects.results: Quest received positive feedback from my girlfriend, its intended user. The app remains private.
